A language-model reviser for the item-revision loop

Source: R/loop-steps.R
loop_reviser_llm.Rd

loop_reviser_llm() makes the reviser step of revision_loop(). After each round, one call shows a language model the construct, every item with its flags and main statistics, the parts of the stopping rule that fail, and the earlier edits with whether they worked. It asks for edits (reword, rekey, drop, add or keep), each with a rationale and the names of the checks it responds to, and one note on the round. These are logged in the edits and rounds tables, so you can see whether the revisions follow the evidence.

Usage

loop_reviser_llm(
  model,
  actions = c("reword", "rekey", "drop", "add", "keep"),
  min_items = 3,
  max_edits = Inf,
  guidelines = lp_guidelines,
  min_total = NULL
)

Arguments

model

an sc_model() for the reviser.

actions

the actions the reviser may take.

min_items

smallest number of items a scale should keep. The model is told, and a drop that would leave a scale with fewer is not applied (the round's reasoning says so).

max_edits

most edits per round, or Inf.

guidelines

item-writing guidelines added to the system prompt.

min_total

smallest number of items in all, or NULL, enforced in the same way.

Value

A function for the reviser argument of revision_loop().

Details

With sc_model("mock"), no model is called: The reviser rewords up to max_edits failing items by adding a word, which is enough to try the loop.

See also

revision_loop(), loop_writer_llm(), loop_reviser_drop()
